name: How do I prevent height and transition problems when replacing kitchen flooring?

mainEntity.name: How do I prevent height and transition problems when replacing kitchen flooring?

acceptedAnswer.text: Floor height should be reviewed wherever the new surface meets cabinets, appliances, doors, baseboards, stairs, or adjacent rooms. A suitable transition may be needed, but excessive height differences can create appearance, clearance, or trip concerns. Context: Removal of thick tile or installation over an existing floor can change the finished elevation in opposite directions. Key factors: - Existing and proposed thickness - Door and appliance clearance - Transition material and location - Cabinet toe-kick relationship Practical guidance: Ask for proposed finished elevations or a transition plan before selecting the product. Elite Remodeling & Design can coordinate these details with cabinet, trim, and layout decisions during kitchen planning.
acceptedAnswer.description: Compare existing and proposed finished heights at cabinets, appliances, doors, and adjoining rooms before installation. Confirm underlayment, transition pieces, toe-kicks, and appliance clearances in the written plan.
